mentions.note: German; joined six months earlier; club's fastest 10 miler; first Belgrave winner of the Garnet since Ray Middleton in 1959

mentions.h: December 22nd - The Horwood Cup 7 miles Junior Championship
mentions.note: won the Horwood Cup 7 miles junior walk, 57.24 - his first championship win
won the Southern Area junior 10 miles walk (Garnet Cup), 77.25
won club 20 miles walking championship (Rickett's Shield), 2.44.53 - his first club championship
won the last 3,000 metres of the season in 12.50.6, fastest by a Belgravian in 1969

mentions.h: July 29th - 6 Mile Race versus Surrey Walking Club - Tooting
November 2nd Belgrave v Civil Service - Imber Court

mentions.note: received the Tommy Green Cup, 21 November 1970

mentions.h: Surrey Championships - SURREY STEEPLECHASE TITLE FOR ALAN BLACK
INTER-COUNTIES - Victory for Surrey in Inter-Counties Championship - Leicester, May 28/30
National 20 m - BACK TO THE DRAWING BOARD
mentions.note: sixth, 2:41:08; last year's winner; had just taken over management of a hotel in Bloomsbury

mentions.h: BACK IN FORM FOR THE LEICESTER MERCURY "20" - May 22, 1971

mentions.note: walked for West Germany in the Olympic 20 kilometres walk, 16th in 1:35:20.6
selected for West Germany in the 20 km walk, Munich Olympics 1972

photos.c: LEFT: Wil Wesch wins the Surrey 10 miles Championship.

Bert East (centre) had difficulty in even making the start of the London Transport '2' on July 6th at Acton, but mention the word "handicap" and he's off like a shot! Ray Middleton thinks it's a laugh beating the 2 miles record of a No.11 bus, while Wil Wesch gets on with winning at well over speed-limit
Wil Wesch (31) in action during the 'Open' 7.
Wil Wesch looks a proud man as he gazes at the Tommy Green Cup, which he received at the Club Dinner and Dance at the Wimbledon Hill Hotel on November 21. Well done Wil.
WIL WESCH (1), selected for West Germany in the 20 Kilos walk at the Olympic Games, Munich 1972, leads British international Paul Nihill in the Surrey County 3,000m track championship of 1971.
